content_voiceover: This is the ASCEMBL trial, the first phase three study to test asciminib against a second generation TKI in patients who had already failed at least two prior TKIs, another new indication highlighted here. Two hundred thirty three adults with chronic phase CML, previously treated with two or more TKIs, who had either failed or were intolerant of their most recent agent, were randomized two to one, asciminib forty milligrams twice daily versus bosutinib five hundred milligrams once daily. Patients were stratified by whether they had achieved major cytogenetic response at baseline. Patients with no T315I or V299L mutations were eligible, since those confer resistance. Notably, if a patient on bosutinib met criteria for lack of efficacy, they were allowed to switch to asciminib, though that crossover population is not part of the current efficacy analysis. Median follow up was two point three years. The primary endpoint was major molecular response at twenty four weeks, with a key secondary endpoint of MMR at ninety six weeks, plus additional secondary endpoints covering cytogenetic response, time to and duration of response, and safety.
keypoints: Two hundred thirty three heavily pretreated CML patients, failed or intolerant of two or more TKIs
Randomized two to one: asciminib forty mg twice daily versus bosutinib five hundred mg daily
Excluded T315I and V299L resistance mutations
Primary endpoint MMR at week 24, key secondary MMR at week 96
keypoint_voiceover: ASCEMBL answers a different clinical question than ASC4FIRST, it is a later line trial, testing asciminib head to head against bosutinib in patients who already failed multiple TKIs. The two to one randomization, stratified by baseline cytogenetic response, and the twenty four week primary MMR endpoint are the design details worth remembering.
